newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Nat'l Bank of Pakistan sees 1996 profit up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nat'l Bank of Pakistan sees 1996 profit up 15 pct.

text.p: The president of the National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) said on Tuesday that its pre-tax profit was expected to rise 15 percent in calendar 1996.
NBP, Pakistan's biggest state-owned bank, increased its pre-tax profit 10 percent to three billion rupees in 1995.
"The bank will close its financial year with greater success than last year in terms of profits and deposits," Abu Saeed Islahi told a news conference.
The caretaker government plans to reform the state financial sector, but says it will not sell NBP, which has 1,550 branches inside and outside Pakistan. NBP has no stock exchange listing.

Islahi said NBP deposits rose to 230 billion rupees in 1996 from 208 billion in 1995. NBP wanted to reduce non-performing loans, which comprised about 13 percent of a loan portfolio of 100 billion rupees and were mostly to ailing textile mills.
He said NBP would appoint an "accountability commissioner" to receive and investigate complaints of corruption.
